John Chrysostom

Icons

Saints

St. John Chrysostom

John the Golden-Mouthed

What is depictedHistory and traditionPublished explanationSources

Dionisius presents St. John Chrysostom as a bishop in a narrow, full-length icon. He holds a Gospel book and wears a light vestment with dark crosses.

[1] Displayed work;file-level title,description,date and visual identification

What is depicted

The bishop’s head inclines and one hand is raised while the other supports the book. The long figure and simple background focus the composition on the identified hierarch. This is Dionisius’s historical depiction, not a portrait claimed to have been painted during John’s lifetime.

[1] Displayed work;file-level title,description,date and visual identification

History and tradition

The file identifies Dionisius as the artist. Its provenance is retained with the original local image and source record. The historical reference excerpt below discusses John’s scriptural interpretation from a named early-twentieth-century Catholic author; its critical terminology is not presented as an Orthodox synodal definition.

[1] Displayed work;file-level title,description,date and visual identification

Published explanation

As an exegete Chrysostom is of the highest importance, for he is the chief and almost the only successful representative of the exegetical principles of the School of Antioch. Diodorus of Tarsus had initiated him into the grammatico-historical method of that school, which was in strong opposition to the eccentric, allegorical, and mystical interpretation of Origen and the Alexandrian School. But Chrysostom rightly avoided pushing his principles to that extreme to which, later on, his friend Theodore of Mopsuestia, the teacher of Nestorius, carried them. He did not even exclude all allegorical or mystical explanations, but confined them to the cases in which the inspired author himself suggests this meaning.

Chrysostom Baur’s historical Catholic Encyclopedia article,original1910 English text. The passage is Baur’s assessment of John’s method,not a quotation spoken by the saint.

[2] Article section on Chrysostom’s exegetical writings
